audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Sylas/Sylas/Skill. The already-audited mirror set this chart to Sylas/Sylas/Sylas/Sylas/Aurora/Sylas/Sylas, and the packet chart agrees.
audit.why: Aurora has no escape before level 2 and cannot walk out of the E-pull once Sylas has his full kit, so the early rows are his; level 6 is hers because Between Worlds outclasses a level-1 Hijack window. Win rate 51.09 over 411 games supports Sylas overall.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 4-5 and Two+ items read Sylas; Level 6 reads Aurora. Proposed as one group with matching ratings and a rewritten phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid text puts Across the Veil at 'roughly 14 seconds pre-CDR'.
audit.why: Riot's cooldown is 22/21/20/19/18s. Telling a player to re-engage after 14 seconds sends him in while her blink is still up — the exact mistake the entry is trying to prevent.
audit.corrected: Stated as 18-22s in mid and in the cooldown breakdown; Between Worlds' 100-140s given as the level-6 punish window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three errors. (a) Her R is called 'Between the Worlds'; the ability is Between Worlds. (b) The R is described as a spirit realm that 'gains range on all abilities inside it' and 'deals heavy burst' — Riot's text gives a leap, a shockwave that damages and slows, and an area that slows and lets Aurora teleport across it, nothing more. (c) Sylas's E is called a stun in whys[1], spikes[0] and wants.foe[0]; Abscond/Abduct has no CC, it pulls him to the target.
audit.why: A wrong R name is unusable, invented R effects make the player fear the wrong thing, and a stun he does not have changes how he commits to every all-in.
audit.corrected: Named Between Worlds; the R restated as shockwave slow plus a slowing zone she can teleport across; every stun replaced with the pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in the entry mentions Grievous Wounds, though Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell and attack that damages you.
audit.why: Her whole attrition plan is passive drain from poke; anti-heal timing is what decides the extended trades the entry tells you to force.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal named in whys[3] as the answer to her drain.

edits.before: Hijack online — you now own a copy of Aurora's ultimate. The all-in math and every 2v2 swing your way.
edits.after: Between Worlds is her level, not yours — bait the cast, then commit on its 100-140s cooldown with your own R up.

edits.after: E Abscond-recast online: bait her 22s Across the Veil with a fake step-up, then dash and recast to pull yourself onto her before she can blink — one clean hook at level 2 sets the tone for the lane.

edits.after: Her 18-22s blink is your clock — re-engage the instant it expires, and buy Grievous Wounds so Spirit Abjuration stops refunding the poke damage you just traded through.

edits.after: Between Worlds is her defining spike: the leap shockwave slows you and the zone it leaves lets her teleport across it, so she resets the fight you thought you had won — bait the cast, then all-in during its 100-140s cooldown.

edits.after: Two items in you are the stronger skirmisher and side-laner; she scales into a teamfight zone-threat but a Hijacked Between Worlds on 30s beats hers on 100s, so keep rotating and convert your lane advantage into map pressure and objectives.

edits.after: E comes online — Abscond's dash into the Abduct pull lets you all-in before Aurora can blink away, and Across the Veil is a 22s cooldown at rank 1.

edits.before: Level 2 changes everything: the moment E unlocks, you have a commit tool she cannot simply walk away from. The key read is her W hop cooldown — it is roughly 14 seconds pre-CDR, so bait it with a fake step-up, then immediately E-dash and recast to hook and stun her. If the hook lands with her W on cooldown, walk W into her face and cleave passive autos; she has no escape and your Kingslayer heal absorbs her retaliation. Levels 3-5 you run this loop on repeat: Q to slow her peel, E to close, W to burst and heal, passive autos in the extended trade. She will try to drift to max Q range between your spell rotations — keep the wave even or slightly pushed so she cannot freeze safely.
edits.after: Level 2 changes everything: the moment E unlocks, you have a commit tool she cannot simply walk away from. The key read is Across the Veil — 22s at rank 1 and still 18s maxed, so bait it with a fake step-up, then E-dash and recast to pull yourself onto her. If the hook lands with her blink down, walk W into her face and cleave passive autos; she has no escape and your Kingslayer heal absorbs her retaliation. Levels 3-5 you run this loop on repeat: Q to slow her, E to close, W to burst and heal, passive autos in the extended trade. She will drift to max Q range between your rotations — keep the wave even or slightly pushed so she cannot freeze safely.

edits.before: At level 6 Aurora's Between the Worlds R becomes a genuine threat — do NOT E into her if she still has R, because the spirit-realm zone deals heavy burst and she can cast Q and passive-drain inside it while you are slowed. Instead, bluff the engage to bait the R, wait the roughly 2-second duration, then E hook and kill her during the cooldown. Stealing her R with Hijack gives you a zone ability you can cast defensively to negate her re-engage. Post-Riftmaker you win any all-in that starts in melee range — the W heal plus Riftmaker omnivamp outheals her poke budget and the stolen R covers your exit. At 2-plus items you remain the stronger side-laner; she is a teamfight carry but you are faster to the map and your stolen R gives your team the same zone threat she would otherwise bring.
edits.after: At level 6 Between Worlds becomes a genuine threat — do NOT E into her while she holds it, because the shockwave slows you and the zone she leaves lets her teleport clean across the fight and reset it. Bluff the engage to bait the cast, let the zone expire, then E hook and kill her during its 100-140s cooldown. Stealing it with Hijack hands you the same slow zone to cut her exit line. Post-Riftmaker you win any all-in that starts in melee range — the W heal plus omnivamp outheals her poke budget, and Grievous Wounds shuts off Spirit Abjuration's drain. At 2-plus items you remain the stronger side-laner; she is a teamfight carry, but your stolen R comes back on 30s and hers does not, so take every fight the moment she spends it.

notes: The invented R effects mattered more than the misspelling here: the entry told the player Between Worlds is a burst zone that extends her ability range, so the whole level-6 fear was aimed at something that does not exist. Riot's text is a leap, a slowing shockwave, and a slow zone she can teleport across. Sylas's E was still described as a stun in three places despite the mirror flagging it. Across the Veil is written as 'Across the Veil (Hop)' throughout the full layer — the parenthetical is clutter but the name is correct, so it was left alone except where a rewrite touched the line anyway.
